day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Transfer from airport to Aegean Bliss Resort, check in, and settle into your room.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Aegean Bliss Resort around 23:30–00:00 after transfer. Grab a light snack from any 24-hour hotel vending area or packed travel snacks. Rest and prepare for the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: N/A — travel day
meals.lunch: N/A — travel day
meals.dinner: Pack airport or in-flight snacks to save money. Alternatively, grab a quick CHF 5–8 sandwich or pastry from an airport kiosk before boarding.

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is late at night. Do not book any transfers that add extra costs — check if the resort offers a complimentary or discounted shuttle from the nearest train station or airport. Confirm check-in arrangements in advance since arrival is after 22:00. Keep luggage light for easy transport through Swiss transit.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely start, head to the resort's base area and rent beginner or intermediate ski equipment from a local rental shop near the resort. Budget ski rentals typically cost CHF 30–45/day. Purchase a half-day lift pass (afternoon) to save money on your first ski day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hit the beginner and intermediate ski slopes near the resort. Stick to well-marked green and blue runs to warm up. Many Swiss Alps resorts have free or low-cost beginner slopes near the base. Explore the surrounding snow-covered terrain and take in the breathtaking Alpine panoramas.
day_by_day.evening: Return ski equipment and stroll through the nearby village. Browse local shops and get oriented with the area. Relax at the hotel and plan the rest of the week.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the hotel if breakfast is included. If not, visit a local bakery (Bäckerei) for fresh bread, croissants, and coffee for CHF 6–10 per person.
meals.lunch: Pack a sandwich and thermos of hot chocolate from a grocery store (Migros or Coop) to eat on the slopes — saves CHF 15–20 vs. mountain restaurant prices.
meals.dinner: Find a local budget-friendly restaurant in the village. Look for a set menu (Tagesmenü) which typically costs CHF 15–22 and includes a main course and sometimes soup or salad. Try rösti (Swiss potato dish) or a hearty Alpine soup.

day_by_day.notes: Buying a multi-day ski pass (3–7 days) is significantly cheaper than daily passes. Check for family discounts — children under 9 often ski free in many Swiss resorts. Rent equipment from off-mountain shops rather than ski school rental counters for better prices.

day_by_day.morning: Full day of skiing! Head to the slopes early (lifts typically open at 08:30–09:00) to avoid crowds. Focus on intermediate blue runs and try one or two red runs if the family is comfortable. Consider a group ski lesson in the morning (CHF 35–50/person for a group lesson vs. CHF 100+ for private) to improve technique.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing after lunch. Explore different lift zones and try a scenic gondola ride to a higher elevation viewpoint even if you ski back down on easier routes. Look for family fun zones with snow tubing or gentle slopes for younger children.
day_by_day.evening: Ice Skating at Davos Ice Stadium — Skate on one of Europe's largest natural outdoor ice rinks set against a stunning mountain backdrop. Admission is typically CHF 6–10 per adult and CHF 4–6 per child. Skate rentals available on-site for approximately CHF 6–8. A magical family evening activity under the Alpine sky.

meals.breakfast: Grocery store run the night before — prepare simple breakfast items like yogurt, fruit, bread, and instant oatmeal in the hotel room to save CHF 10–15 per person.
meals.lunch: Mountain hut (Bergrestaurant) lunch — treat yourself to one mountain meal this trip. Order a shared fondue or a bowl of goulash soup (CHF 8–12) rather than a full meal to keep costs down.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using the hotel kitchenette if available, OR visit a Migros or Coop supermarket deli counter for ready-made meals (CHF 8–12 per person). Swiss supermarkets have excellent hot and cold prepared foods.

day_by_day.notes: Davos Ice Stadium is one of the highlights of the Swiss Alps winter experience. Check opening hours in advance as they can vary by season and weather. The rink may be partially covered or fully outdoor depending on conditions. Bring warm gloves and an extra layer for the evening skating session.

day_by_day.morning: Rest day from skiing — explore the local Alpine village on foot. Take a free self-guided walking tour of the town center, admire traditional Swiss chalets, and visit a local church or historic building. Many Swiss Alpine villages have free heritage trails with informational signs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Winter hiking on a marked snow trail (Winterwanderweg). Most Swiss Alpine resorts maintain free or low-cost groomed walking paths separate from ski slopes. Rent snowshoes for CHF 10–15/day and explore the forest and meadow trails with spectacular mountain views. Suitable for all fitness levels and great for families.
day_by_day.evening: Warm up at the hotel with a board game night or family relaxation time. Alternatively, visit a local community center or sports hall — many Swiss Alpine towns host free or low-cost evening events in winter season.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local bakery. Try a Gipfeli (Swiss croissant) with butter and jam — a classic Alpine start for CHF 3–5.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch on the winter hiking trail. Pack sandwiches, cheese, Swiss chocolate, and hot drinks from a thermos. Buy supplies from Coop or Migros the evening before.
meals.dinner: Budget restaurant dinner — look for a Pizzeria or Italian restaurant in the village (common throughout Swiss Alps) where a pizza or pasta dish runs CHF 14–20. Share a bottle of local Swiss mineral water instead of ordering individual drinks.

day_by_day.notes: A rest day mid-week prevents ski fatigue and muscle soreness, especially for children. Winter hiking is free or very low cost and offers some of the most beautiful scenery in the Alps without lift pass costs. Always check trail conditions and carry a basic first aid kit and extra warm layers.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the ski slopes for another full day. Focus on trying runs you haven't done yet. Challenge yourself with a longer red run or explore a different mountain sector accessible with your lift pass. Arrive early to beat weekend crowds that start arriving Friday afternoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snow tubing or sledding (Schlitteln) — many Swiss Alpine resorts have dedicated sledding runs (Schlittelbahn) that are free or very low cost (CHF 5–10 for sled rental). This is a fantastic family activity that children absolutely love and is far cheaper than skiing.
day_by_day.evening: Fondue night! Visit a local restaurant for a traditional Swiss cheese fondue. Many restaurants offer a fondue set for CHF 22–28 per person — it's a cultural must-do and very filling. Look for set menus or early-bird specials to reduce cost. Share one pot between two people to save money.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or bakery breakfast. Fuel up well for a full ski day.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the slopes again — by now you should have a system down. Hot soup in a thermos is a game-changer on cold ski days.
meals.dinner: Traditional Swiss cheese fondue at a local restaurant (CHF 22–28/person). Drink tap water (Leitungswasser) which is perfectly safe and free in Switzerland, saving CHF 4–6 per person on drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Friday afternoons get busier on slopes as weekend visitors arrive. Plan to finish skiing by 15:00 to avoid lift queues. Sledding runs are often free to access and provide hours of entertainment for children. Confirm fondue restaurant reservations in advance as popular spots fill up quickly on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Cross-country skiing (Langlauf) — a fantastic budget-friendly alternative to downhill skiing. Trail passes are significantly cheaper (CHF 5–15 vs. CHF 50–80 for downhill lift passes) and cross-country ski rentals are also more affordable (CHF 15–25/day). Explore beautifully groomed Nordic trails through snowy forests and meadows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local Swiss Alpine museum or visitor center (often free or CHF 3–5 entry) to learn about the region's history, culture, and Alpine traditions. Alternatively, spend the afternoon at a free outdoor snow play area — build snowmen, have snowball fights, and enjoy the mountains without spending a franc.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Davos Ice Stadium for a second evening skate session if the family loved it on Day 3, or explore the village's winter market stalls if any are operating. Pick up affordable Swiss souvenirs like small chocolate bars (CHF 2–4), postcards (CHF 1–2), or local jam.

meals.breakfast: Supermarket breakfast — buy a selection of Swiss cheeses, cold cuts, bread, and fresh juice from Migros or Coop for a proper Swiss-style breakfast in the room for CHF 5–7 per person.
meals.lunch: Warm up at a mountain hut café with a hot chocolate (CHF 4–5) and a shared plate of Älplermagronen (Swiss Alpine mac and cheese with applesauce) — a hearty, affordable mountain classic around CHF 14–18.
meals.dinner: Self-catering dinner — cook pasta or a simple meal in the hotel room/kitchenette. Buy ingredients at the supermarket for CHF 5–8 per person total. This is the biggest money-saver of the trip.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is the busiest day on downhill ski slopes — deliberately choosing cross-country skiing avoids crowds entirely and saves significant money. Swiss supermarkets (Migros, Coop, Lidl) are the best budget tools in Switzerland — shop there for snacks, drinks, and meals whenever possible. Lidl and Aldi are the cheapest options if available in the area.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning ski session — use the last of your multi-day lift pass if applicable. Focus on favorite runs and take plenty of photos and videos to capture memories. Return rental equipment by the designated time (usually before 17:00 but confirm with rental shop).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort (standard checkout is 11:00–12:00 — store luggage with reception if needed). Take a leisurely final walk through the Alpine village. Visit a local chocolate shop or cheese shop for affordable take-home gifts. Enjoy one last look at the stunning Swiss mountain scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Depart for the airport or next destination. Allow extra time for Swiss transit connections — trains are punctual but mountain resort transfers can take 1.5–2.5 hours to major airports. Grab a final meal at the train station or airport.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or bakery visit — treat the family to a proper sit-down breakfast as a trip celebration. Budget CHF 8–12 per person.
meals.lunch: Light lunch from supermarket or bakery before checkout. Use up any remaining groceries purchased during the week.
meals.dinner: Train station or airport meal — look for Migros or Coop To Go outlets inside Swiss train stations which offer excellent quality ready meals, sandwiches, and hot food at reasonable prices (CHF 8–14 per person) — far better value than airport restaurants.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with the resort and arrange luggage storage if your departure is in the late afternoon or evening. Swiss Federal Railways (SBB) trains are the most reliable and often most cost-effective way to reach airports — book tickets in advance online for Supersaver fares. Keep CHF 20–30 per person as a buffer for unexpected transport or meal costs on departure day. Overall budget tip: A family of 4 can realistically experience the Swiss Alps on CHF 150–200/day total (excluding accommodation) by using supermarkets, group lessons, multi-day passes, and free activities.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Transfer from airport to Aegean Bliss Resort, Swiss Alps. Check in, settle into your Beachfront room, and get a good night's rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Aegean Bliss Resort around 23:30–00:00 after transfer. Light welcome snack at the hotel if available, then rest and prepare for the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: Meal on flight or airport snack before departure
meals.lunch: Meal on flight or at departure airport
meals.dinner: Light late-night snack at hotel upon arrival — many Alpine resorts offer 24-hour reception with cold platters or vending options

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 completely free of planned activities. Confirm transfer booking in advance. Pack ski gear in checked luggage or arrange rental upon arrival. Set an alarm for a fresh start on Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely hotel breakfast to recover from travel. After breakfast, head to the resort's ski rental or nearby ski shop to fit the whole family with proper ski equipment, boots, and helmets. Purchase lift passes for the Jungfrau Ski Region. Beginners and children can register for a morning group ski lesson with a certified instructor.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hit the slopes at the Jungfrau Ski Region — enjoy 213km of groomed pistes across all skill levels. Families can explore the dedicated beginner zones while more confident skiers tackle intermediate blue and red runs. Take a mid-afternoon break at a mountain-top restaurant for hot chocolate and a rest before one final run down.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel, freshen up, and explore the resort village on foot. Browse local Alpine souvenir shops and enjoy the charming winter atmosphere of the Swiss Alps village center.

meals.breakfast: Full buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — included or mid-range hotel dining option
meals.lunch: Mountain-top ski hut lunch on the slopes — try a classic Swiss rösti with a warm soup (budget ~CHF 20–30 per person)
meals.dinner: Cozy mid-range Alpine restaurant in the village — order traditional cheese fondue or raclette for a true Swiss welcome dinner (budget ~CHF 35–50 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book ski lessons in advance, especially for children, as slots fill up quickly during peak February season. Dress in moisture-wicking base layers, insulated mid-layers, and a waterproof outer shell. Apply high-SPF sunscreen — Alpine sun reflects off snow intensely.

day_by_day.morning: Full day on the Jungfrau Ski Region slopes. Start early to beat crowds and enjoy freshly groomed morning pistes. Intermediate and advanced skiers can tackle the more challenging red and black runs, while younger family members continue group or private ski lessons to build confidence.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, switch gears and head to the Snow Tubing and Sledding at Faulhorn — experience one of Europe's longest natural toboggan runs stretching over 15km from Faulhorn down to Grindelwald. This is a fantastic family activity that requires no prior skill and delivers pure adrenaline and laughter for all ages.
day_by_day.evening: Warm up back at the hotel with a visit to the spa or heated pool if available at Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a relaxed family evening with board games or a movie in the lounge area.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast buffet — fuel up well before a full active day
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or quick bite at a slope-side snack bar — sandwiches, energy bars, and warm drinks (budget ~CHF 15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant dinner or a nearby mid-range Alpine bistro — try Zürcher Geschnetzeltes (Zurich-style veal) or a hearty Alpine pasta dish (budget ~CHF 30–45 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Faulhorn toboggan run is weather-dependent and may require pre-booking sleds. Check conditions the night before. Wear waterproof trousers and gloves for sledding — you will get wet! Children must be accompanied by an adult on the longer toboggan sections.

day_by_day.morning: Take a break from skiing and embark on the legendary Glacier Express Scenic Train Ride — a family-friendly panoramic rail journey through dramatic Alpine landscapes, crossing 291 bridges and passing through 91 tunnels. Book the morning departure for the best light and visibility. Enjoy the breathtaking views of snow-capped peaks, frozen rivers, and charming Swiss villages from panoramic windows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark at a scenic midpoint stop or complete a portion of the route before returning. Explore the stop-off town, visit a local artisan shop, or enjoy a walk along a snow-covered promenade before boarding the return train.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Swiss Alps base and enjoy a cultural evening with the Swiss Alpine Cheese and Fondue Cultural Experience — a guided visit to a traditional Alpine cheese dairy where you learn how Swiss mountain cheese is made, followed by a hands-on fondue cooking session with local ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before catching the morning Glacier Express departure
meals.lunch: Dining car on the Glacier Express — a classic Swiss rail lunch experience with regional specialties and scenic views (budget ~CHF 35–50 per person, pre-bookable)
meals.dinner: Fondue dinner included as part of the Swiss Alpine Cheese and Fondue Cultural Experience — authentic and memorable (budget ~CHF 45–60 per person including the experience)

day_by_day.notes: Glacier Express seats must be reserved well in advance, especially during February peak season. Book panoramic window seats for the best views. The cheese and fondue experience typically lasts 2–3 hours and is highly interactive for children — a highlight of any Swiss Alps trip.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the Jungfrau Ski Region for a full morning ski session. By Day 5, the family will have developed significantly more confidence on the slopes. Challenge yourselves with new runs you haven't tried yet — perhaps a longer red run or a scenic off-piste route with a qualified guide. Take the Jungfraujoch cable car to the 'Top of Europe' for panoramic views at 3,454m altitude.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Ice Skating at Davos Ice Stadium — skate on one of Europe's largest natural outdoor ice rinks set against a stunning mountain backdrop. Rental skates are available on-site. This is a relaxed, fun activity perfect for the whole family after an energetic morning on the slopes.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the Davos village or return to your resort area for a relaxed evening. Visit a local Alpine spa for a post-activity recovery session — many offer family packages with saunas, steam rooms, and heated pools.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — try to include protein-rich options like eggs and cheese to fuel a big activity day
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at a Davos café or mountain restaurant near the ice stadium — try a Swiss-style Wurstsalat (sausage salad) or a warm Käseschnitte (cheese toast) (budget ~CHF 20–30 per person)
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant dinner back near the resort — try a traditional Swiss Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup) starter followed by grilled Alpine trout or Älplermagronen (Alpine mac and cheese) (budget ~CHF 35–50 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Davos is approximately 1.5–2 hours from the Jungfrau region — confirm travel logistics the night before. The Jungfraujoch excursion adds ~CHF 100–150 per adult and requires separate tickets. At altitude, altitude sickness can affect some visitors — stay hydrated and ascend slowly.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated family ski day — spend the entire morning on the Jungfrau Ski Region pistes. Today is about applying everything learned during the week. Attempt a family ski run together on a blue or green route, creating lasting memories. More advanced family members can explore higher-altitude runs while others enjoy a relaxed ski at their own pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, enjoy a guided snowshoe walk or a family-friendly winter hiking trail near the resort. Many Swiss Alpine resorts offer marked winter walking paths through snowy forests with stunning mountain views — no special equipment needed beyond warm boots and poles. Alternatively, visit a local Alpine village for a cultural afternoon walk and hot chocolate stop.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Swiss Alps dinner — celebrate a wonderful week in the mountains with a special dinner at one of the resort's best restaurants or a highly-rated local Alpine establishment. Reflect on the week's adventures as a family.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — leisurely start to the final full day
meals.lunch: Slope-side mountain restaurant lunch — splurge slightly on a sit-down meal with Alpine views. Try a cheese soup, local sausages, and Appenzeller beer for adults (budget ~CHF 30–40 per person)
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at a top-rated local Alpine restaurant — try a three-course meal with Swiss classics: Bündnerfleisch (air-dried beef) starter, Veal Zurich-style main, and Meringue with double cream dessert (budget ~CHF 55–75 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday slopes can be busier with weekend visitors — head out early (first lifts open around 8:30am) to enjoy quieter morning conditions. Book the farewell dinner reservation in advance. Consider purchasing Swiss Alpine chocolate, cheese, and local jams as take-home gifts from village shops this afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely morning at Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a relaxed hotel breakfast without rushing. Take a short walk around the resort grounds or village to soak in the Alpine scenery one last time. Pack luggage and check out of the hotel. If time allows before checkout, visit the hotel spa for a final relaxation session.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, enjoy a final light activity — a short snowshoe walk, a visit to a local Alpine museum, or simply a warm café stop with Swiss pastries and coffee. Begin transfer to the airport with plenty of time to spare for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Switzerland with incredible family memories of world-class skiing, scenic train journeys, cultural fondue experiences, and the breathtaking beauty of the Swiss Alps. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — enjoy all your favorites from the week
meals.lunch: Light lunch at an airport café or a final village café stop before departure — try a Swiss pretzel, Gipfeli (Swiss croissant), or a Birchermüesli (budget ~CHF 15–25 per person)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant dinner or in-flight meal depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Swiss International Air Lines and major carriers operate from Zurich (ZRH) and Geneva (GVA) airports. Allow at least 3 hours before international flight departure for check-in, security, and Swiss customs. Ski equipment check-in may require extra time — arrive early. Declare any food items (cheese, meat) at customs when returning home.

meals.lunch: Gourmet dining car experience aboard the Glacier Express — three-course lunch featuring seasonal Swiss ingredients with panoramic mountain views rolling past the windows
meals.dinner: Private in-suite or private dining room fondue experience — three-cheese fondue with premium accompaniments, charcuterie, and a curated Swiss wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Reserve first-class Glacier Express seats well in advance as they sell out quickly. The concierge can arrange seamless transfers to and from the train station. Bring layers as temperatures vary between the train and outdoor stops.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Faulhorn for the world-renowned Snow Tubing and Sledding experience — one of Europe's longest natural toboggan runs stretching over 15km. The entire family will enjoy the thrilling descent through pristine Alpine scenery. Private guide accompanies the family for safety and the best route selection.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the exhilarating toboggan run, warm up with hot chocolate and Alpine pastries at a cozy mountain hut. In the afternoon, return to the Jungfrau Ski Region for a relaxed family ski session, focusing on fun runs and confidence-building for younger family members with the private ski instructor.
day_by_day.evening: Spa and wellness evening at the resort — book the family spa suite for a private session including hot stone massages, steam room, and Alpine herb treatments. Dinner at a renowned local Alpine restaurant in the village.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet — extended leisurely breakfast with Swiss granola, warm pastries, smoked salmon, and premium coffee blends
meals.lunch: Traditional mountain hut lunch near Faulhorn — hearty Alpine soup, Käseschnitten (Swiss cheese toast), and warm apple strudel with cream
meals.dinner: Dinner at a premium local Alpine restaurant — venison medallions, truffle risotto, and seasonal Alpine vegetables paired with a curated Swiss red wine selection

day_by_day.notes: The Faulhorn toboggan run requires advance booking during peak season. Dress in waterproof layers as snow tubing and sledding can be wet. The resort spa should be pre-booked to secure the private family suite time slot.

day_by_day.morning: Immerse the family in authentic Swiss mountain culture with the Swiss Alpine Cheese and Fondue Cultural Experience — a guided visit to a traditional Alpine cheese dairy where a master cheesemaker walks the family through centuries-old cheesemaking techniques. Includes a tasting of aged Gruyère, Emmental, and Appenzeller cheeses.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the cultural experience with a guided Alpine village walk and visit to a local artisan workshop. In the late afternoon, enjoy a private snowshoe hike through pristine winter forest trails with a certified mountain guide — a peaceful contrast to the high-energy ski days.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a celebratory family dinner at the resort's fine dining restaurant. Request a chef's table experience where the executive chef personally presents each course — a luxurious and memorable culinary highlight of the trip.

meals.breakfast: In-suite breakfast — freshly prepared Swiss rösti with eggs, smoked meats, artisan breads, and a selection of local mountain honeys and jams
meals.lunch: Farm-to-table lunch at the cheese dairy — freshly made cheese fondue, homemade bread, Alpine charcuterie, and locally brewed herbal tea
meals.dinner: Chef's table experience at Aegean Bliss Resort's fine dining restaurant — seven-course tasting menu with wine pairing, featuring Alpine-inspired haute cuisine crafted with seasonal Swiss ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the cheese dairy cultural experience through the resort concierge as group sizes are limited. The snowshoe hike is suitable for children aged 6 and above. Chef's table reservations should be made at least 48 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Full day at the Jungfrau Ski Region — the family's most ambitious ski day. With several days of practice, tackle more challenging runs with the private ski instructor. Advanced family members can explore the higher-altitude black runs while beginners continue progressing on blue and red pistes. Ride the Jungfraujoch cable car to the 'Top of Europe' for breathtaking panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch on the mountain, the afternoon is dedicated to Ice Skating at Davos Ice Stadium — one of Europe's largest natural outdoor ice rinks set against a stunning mountain backdrop. Private ice skating session arranged with a professional coach for the family. Skate hire and warm-up hot beverages included.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-eve celebration dinner at the most prestigious restaurant in the area — a Michelin-starred Alpine dining experience. Pre-arrange a surprise dessert presentation for the family to celebrate a wonderful trip.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast buffet — fuel up with a protein-rich spread including eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, fresh fruit, yogurt parfaits, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Summit restaurant lunch at Jungfraujoch or Kleine Scheidegg — premium Alpine cuisine at altitude with sweeping glacier views, including Alplermagronen (Alpine mac and cheese) and warm soups
meals.dinner: Michelin-starred restaurant dinner — signature tasting menu celebrating regional Alpine ingredients including game, truffles, and artisan Swiss produce, with sommelier-guided wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The Jungfraujoch cable car experience requires advance booking, especially during peak February ski season. Davos Ice Stadium is approximately a transfer away — arrange private luxury vehicle with the resort. Dress warmly for outdoor ice skating as temperatures at the rink can be significantly colder.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely morning at the resort. Enjoy a slow, indulgent farewell breakfast. Take a peaceful last walk through the Alpine village or along the resort's snow-lined grounds. Visit the resort gift shop to pick up premium Swiss souvenirs — artisan chocolates, Alpine honey, and Swiss timepieces.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the resort with full concierge assistance for luggage and transfers. Private luxury transfer to the airport for departure. Enjoy a final Swiss treat at the airport's premium lounge before boarding.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry the memories of an extraordinary Swiss Alpine luxury family adventure.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort — the full buffet experience featuring every Swiss specialty enjoyed during the week, including a made-to-order crêpe station and premium Swiss hot chocolate
meals.lunch: Light gourmet bites at the airport's premium lounge or a quick upscale café near the resort before transfer — Swiss open-faced sandwiches, fresh fruit, and artisan pastries
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or upon arrival at home destination

day_by_day.notes: Request a 12:00 noon or later check-out from the resort to maximize the final morning. Confirm private transfer timing with the concierge the evening before. Ensure all ski equipment rentals are returned and resort charges are settled the night prior to avoid morning delays. Pre-pack Swiss chocolate and specialty food items carefully to comply with customs regulations.
